# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 24 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 24 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_024_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 24

**24:1** Now I, James, who wrote this history — when the tumult arose in Jerusalem at the death of Herod, I withdrew into the wilderness until the tumult in Jerusalem had ceased. I glorified the Lord God who gave me the wisdom to write this history.

**24:2** And grace shall be with all those who fear the Lord. Amen.

---

## Translator's Note

This penultimate chapter is the authorial colophon, where "James" — the purported author — steps into the narrative for the first time, breaking the frame of the story. The claim that James withdrew to the wilderness at Herod's death is a pseudepigraphical device creating biographical plausibility: James, as the brother of the Lord, would have reason to flee at the Massacre of the Innocents period. The "grace to all who fear the Lord" is a standard epistolary benediction formula, positioning this text as a spiritual gift to its readership. The chapter division here varies significantly between MSS; many traditions combine this with what is here called ch. 25 as a single closing.
